name: Google Agent Platform Sandbox (Code Execution / Shell / Computer Use)

modes.label: Code Execution / Shell sandbox (API exec, same Agent Compute + Agent Memory meter)
modes.note: Same published meter ($0.085/vCPU-h + $0.009/GiB-h allocated, per-second). Code Execution: Python or JavaScript (LANGUAGE_PYTHON / LANGUAGE_JAVASCRIPT), two fixed shapes (default 2 vCPU/1.5 GB, or 4 vCPU/4 GB), "limited file system and no network access", preinstalled libraries only ("You can't install your own libraries"), no snapshots, state kept up to 14 days (TTL configurable; execute_code resets the TTL). Shell sandbox: "a managed, isolated Linux container" reached through an /exec API, not SSH; its vCPU/RAM shape is not published.

modes.label: Computer Use sandbox (managed browser, billed as Agent Compute + Agent Memory)
modes.note: Pricing page (2026-09-28): "Runtime and Sandbox environments, including Code Execution and Computer Use, are billed on Agent Compute (vCPU-hours) and Agent Memory (GiB-hours)... vCPU resources allocated... $0.085/vCPU-h... Memory (RAM) resources allocated... $0.009/GiB-h. All usage is rounded to the nearest second." This regime is the Computer Use sandbox: a containerized browser driven via API actions / Chrome DevTools Protocol with a VNC live view. Not an SSH VM; a full desktop beyond the browser is not documented.

modes.label: Computer Use / Shell sandbox on Gemini Enterprise Flexible Savings Plan (1 year)
modes.commit_note: Spend-based 1-year Flexible Savings Plan (consumption model 7754-699E-0EBF per page); opt-in; commitment amount/minimum not stated on pricing page.
modes.note: Pricing page Flexible Savings Plan 1-Year column: 10% off Agent Compute and Agent Memory.

modes.label: Computer Use / Shell sandbox on Gemini Enterprise Flexible Savings Plan (3 year)
modes.commit_note: Spend-based 3-year Flexible Savings Plan; opt-in; commitment amount/minimum not stated on pricing page.
modes.note: Pricing page Flexible Savings Plan 3-Year column: 20% off Agent Compute and Agent Memory.

plans.name: Usage based
plans.note: Unknown limits are not promises of unlimited capacity.

features.ip_note: Computer Use sandbox only (code-execution sandbox has no network); runs in Google Cloud, no proxy/stealth/CAPTCHA options documented; screen API covers the browser, not a full OS desktop.

caveats: One meter, three sandbox types: Agent Compute $0.085/vCPU-h + Agent Memory $0.009/GiB-h (allocated, per-second) covers Agent Runtime, Code Execution, Shell and Computer Use sandboxes (Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, formerly Vertex AI Agent Engine). The Runtime idle-between-turns exemption applies to Runtime only, not to sandboxes.

None of these is an SSH-able VM: Computer Use is a containerized browser (API actions / CDP / VNC view); Code Execution is Python-only with no network access; Shell sandbox runs commands through an API. Sandbox vCPU/RAM sizes are not published.

ENGINE_CARD cannot apply all independent free CPU/RAM/storage/request allowances exactly. Raw regimes/worked example retain them; any engine subtotal may overstate charges or miss eligibility. Do not subtract them twice.

Features set to null were not verified. No sandbox was purchased or tested; feature/performance statements are documentation claims. Null maximums are unknown unless a cited note explicitly states unlimited.
A complete monthly bill requires known snapshot/egress/plan limits; do not silently treat missing ancillary charges as free.

fleet.verification: Google Cloud project, billing and required Agent Platform IAM/API setup.
fleet.tiers: Per project per region: 1,000 sandbox entities; 500 sandbox write (create/delete/update) requests/min; 1,000 execute requests/min; 10 Agent Platform resource (instance) writes/min; 100 Agent Platform resources.
fleet.notes: Computer Use sandbox quickstart is distinct from Code Execution. Reviewed quota page labels 1,000 sandbox entities specifically Code Execution; do not automatically assign that as Computer Use concurrent-machine allowance. New-account fleet quota/increase process not established.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_on_demand.quote: Save the exact state of the sandbox, including installed libraries, file system changes, and memory state.
snapshot_on_demand.note: Memory included. SDK client.sandboxes.snapshots.create with a TTL; restore by creating a new sandbox with sandbox_environment_snapshot; 'Branching: Create multiple sandboxes from the same snapshot' (fork). Same image/arch/runtime version required. Not supported for Code Execution sandboxes ('Snapshots are not supported for Code Execution sandboxes').

harness_api.quote: The simplest way to use Managed Agents API on Agent Platform is to interact directly with the first-party Antigravity base agent.
harness_api.note: Managed Agents API (Pre-GA, runs on the Agent Platform sandbox environment): Interactions API starts the Antigravity harness (base_agent antigravity-preview-05-2026) with a prompt, streams SSE events, continues via previous_interaction_id and reuses the sandbox via environment_id; Agents API creates/lists/deletes agent configs. Only Google's own Antigravity harness; no Claude Code/Codex. The plain Code Execution/Shell/Computer Use sandboxes only have exec/browser-action APIs.

egress_allowlist.quote: By default, the sandbox operates without external network access. Explicitly enable connectivity by setting a domain allowlist in your environment configuration.
egress_allowlist.note: Managed Agents: domain allowlist, default-deny. Sandbox templates: egress_control_config.internet_access on/off ('Outbound internet access is off unless the template enables it', shell quickstart). With PSC-I, egress is bridged into your VPC and governed by Cloud NGFW rules (FQDN objects + IP ranges, default-deny) per configure-vpc-sc page. All enforced outside the container.

egress_http_rules.quote: deploy Secure Web Proxy as the egress inspection point in your VPC for TLS-aware, per-URL policy
egress_http_rules.note: Only via PSC-I egress into your own VPC plus Google Cloud Secure Web Proxy (separately billed GCP product); not a sandbox-native setting.

ingress_rules.quote: Reach that data plane over a private Private Service Connect endpoint (PSC-E) in your VPC instead of over the public internet.
ingress_rules.note: Private ingress via PSC-E limited to the same project; template declares which container ports are exposed; data-plane/CDP access requires IAM-generated WebSocket headers (generate_browser_ws_headers with a service account).

guest_firewall.quote: Security: Must not require root privileges or access to restricted system resources, as the image will run within a secure, isolated sandbox.
guest_firewall.note: Containerized sandbox (underlying Agent Substrate runs actors under gVisor or cloud-hypervisor microVMs); images must run without root, so in-guest iptables/nftables is not expected to be available. Not tested.

isolation.quote: A shell sandbox is a managed, isolated Linux container attached to an Agent Platform instance.
isolation.note: Custom-container (BYOC) docs likewise describe the sandbox as a container image run 'within a secure, isolated sandbox' without root privileges.

image_oci.quote: you can provide your own container images (also known as bring your own container or BYOC)... Add image to Artifact Registry: Add your image to Google Cloud Artifact Registry where Agent Platform can access it.
image_oci.note: Image must come from Artifact Registry, be Linux-based, and must not require root.

docker_inside.quote: Commands run as the unprivileged user appuser; there is no sudo.
docker_inside.note: derived: no root/sudo inside the container and custom images 'must not require root privileges', so running a Docker daemon inside is not expected to work; not documented either way.

nested_virt.quote: Security: Must not require root privileges or access to restricted system resources, as the image will run within a secure, isolated sandbox.
nested_virt.note: derived: no root/KVM access documented inside the unprivileged container sandbox.

desktop.quote: Computer Use sandboxes support a live streaming view (VNC), letting you to visually monitor the agent's actions in real-time.
desktop.note: not offered: the VNC/screenshot view covers the managed browser only ('a secure, isolated browser environment'), not a full OS desktop.

anti_bot.quote: Agent Platform Computer Use sandboxes provide a secure, isolated browser environment that your agents can interact with.
anti_bot.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; no stealth/fingerprinting-evasion features are documented.

captcha_solving.quote: Agent Platform Computer Use sandboxes provide a secure, isolated browser environment that your agents can interact with.
captcha_solving.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; no CAPTCHA-solving feature is documented.

snapshot_auto.quote: To create a snapshot of a sandbox, use the Python SDK: ... snapshot_operation = client.sandboxes.snapshots.create(...)
snapshot_auto.note: Snapshots and pause/resume both require an explicit SDK/API call; nothing is saved/restored automatically on stop or timeout.

fork_running.quote: Branching: Create multiple sandboxes from the same snapshot to explore different paths or test variations.
fork_running.note: Snapshot creation targets a sandbox by name without requiring it be paused first, so branching from a running sandbox is supported; original sandbox keeps running unaffected.

memory_snapshot_fork.quote: Save the exact state of the sandbox, including installed libraries, file system changes, and memory state.
memory_snapshot_fork.note: Snapshots (used for branching into new sandboxes) explicitly include memory state, not just disk.

wake_on_request.quote: Transition to STATE_PAUSED. Requests to their data-plane endpoint return errors until you resume.
wake_on_request.note: A paused sandbox must be explicitly resumed via API; incoming requests do not auto-wake it.

persistent_disk.quote: Retain all in-container file system state at the moment of pause.
persistent_disk.note: Filesystem state survives pause/resume (the sandbox's stop/start cycle); no separate 'stopped-but-not-paused' state is documented.

volume_attach.quote: you can provide your own container images... This feature lets you run custom workloads within the secure confines of a sandbox environment.
volume_attach.note: not offered: no attachable extra persistent volume is documented; sandboxes only have their own container filesystem.

volume_shared.quote: you can provide your own container images... This feature lets you run custom workloads within the secure confines of a sandbox environment.
volume_shared.note: not offered: no volume shareable across multiple running sandboxes is documented.

live_resize.quote: To change an existing sandbox's configuration, you must delete it and create a new one.

agent_harnesses.quote: The simplest way to use Managed Agents API on Agent Platform is to interact directly with the first-party Antigravity base agent.
agent_harnesses.note: The only preinstalled agent is Google's own Antigravity base agent; no third-party coding harnesses like Claude Code, Codex, or OpenCode are offered as templates.

own_agent_api.quote: You'll learn how to engage with custom agents built using the Agents API and the prebuilt Antigravity base agent, including configuring it dynamically.
own_agent_api.note: not offered: the only first-party managed-agent product documented is Antigravity, a coding/dev harness (an ADK/'base agent'), not a browser/computer-use or research task agent; the Computer Use sandbox itself only exposes raw action/CDP APIs, no first-party agent driving it.

mcp_server.quote: A common use case is dynamically overriding connections to Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers at runtime.
mcp_server.note: MCP is referenced only as a client-side tool spec that agents can connect to (bring-your-own MCP servers); no evidence the provider ships its own MCP server for controlling its sandboxes.

lang_node.quote: Only LANGUAGE_PYTHON and LANGUAGE_JAVASCRIPT are supported.
lang_node.note: Code Execution sandbox supports JavaScript in addition to Python.

public_ipv4.quote: Enable private ingress with Private Service Connect (PSC-E)... Private ingress can be enabled for exactly one consumer project, and it must be the same user project the sandbox runs in.
public_ipv4.note: Sandbox ingress is via private PSC endpoints/IAM-signed WebSocket connections, not a public IPv4 address.

inbound_https.quote: The sandbox exposes an interactive data plane and makes outbound calls, so it is governed with two Private Service Connect controls: private ingress (PSC-E) and egress control (PSC-I).
inbound_https.note: No public HTTPS URL to reach a sandbox port is documented; access is via a private PSC endpoint or an IAM-authenticated CDP/WebSocket connection.

secret_proxy.quote: MCP credentials scoping: Header configurations for Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, which contain backend authentication tokens, are transmitted only when accessing the specific MCP endpoints defined in your configuration.
secret_proxy.note: This scoping only limits when configured MCP-server tokens are sent; it is not a general first-party proxy that injects credentials for arbitrary HTTP APIs.

gpu.quote: Runtime and Sandbox environments, including Code Execution and Computer Use, are billed on Agent Compute (vCPU-hours) and Agent Memory (GiB-hours) resource usage.
gpu.note: Sandbox pricing/sizes are CPU+RAM only (fixed shapes 2vCPU/1.5GB or 4vCPU/4GB); no GPU option is documented for Code Execution/Shell/Computer Use sandboxes.

arm64.quote: You cannot restore a sandbox snapshot to a new sandbox environment if any of the following conditions are true: The new sandbox uses a different server architecture (for example, amd64 versus arm64).
arm64.note: Implies arm64 is an available sandbox server architecture alongside amd64; not otherwise separately documented as a selectable option.

self_host.quote: Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform... Unified platform for ML models, generative AI, and agent building.
self_host.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; this is a fully managed Google Cloud service, not software you run on your own infrastructure.

byoc.quote: Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform... Unified platform for ML models, generative AI, and agent building.
byoc.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; sandboxes run in Google Cloud's own infrastructure, not deployed into the customer's cloud account.

open_source.quote: Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform... Unified platform for ML models, generative AI, and agent building.
open_source.note: not offered: proprietary managed Google Cloud service; core sandbox implementation is not published under an OSI license.

soc2.quote: Google Cloud regularly undergoes third-party audits for our products, systems, and infrastructure related to this standard.
soc2.note: Core Google Cloud SOC 2 Type II reports cover the platform broadly; Agent Platform is listed as a featured Google Cloud product on the compliance offerings page, but the sandbox sub-feature is not separately named in the SOC 2 scope list retrieved.

hipaa.quote: Covered Products ... Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform
hipaa.note: Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform is explicitly listed among Google Cloud's HIPAA-covered products (BAA available).

sso.quote: Single sign-on: Whenever a user needs to authenticate, Google Cloud delegates the authentication to Active Directory by using the Security Assertion Markup Language (SAML) protocol.
sso.note: SAML/OIDC SSO is a Google Cloud platform-wide capability (via Cloud Identity/Workspace federation) covering console/API access to Agent Platform; not a sandbox-specific feature page.

root.quote: Commands run as the unprivileged user appuser; there is no sudo.
root.note: Shell sandbox explicitly runs as unprivileged appuser with no sudo. Custom-containers page also requires images to run without root ('Must not require root privileges... as the image will run within a secure, isolated sandbox'). No mode documents a root/sudo option.

ssh.quote: A shell sandbox is a managed, isolated Linux container attached to an Agent Platform instance. The sandbox runs a shell command sent by your agent and returns stdout, stderr, and an exit code.
ssh.note: Shell sandbox is reached only via an API-driven exec call (one-shot commands, no persistent shell session), Code Execution runs Python/JS via API, and Computer Use is driven via API actions/CDP with a VNC view. No mode documents an SSH endpoint or key-based SSH access anywhere in the docs.

auto_stop_idle.quote: Pausing a sandbox releases its compute resources while preserving disk state and connection metadata. ... Use pause when a sandbox is idle for an extended period but you want to preserve session state and connection identity for later use.
auto_stop_idle.note: Pause is an explicit API call (client.sandboxes.pause(...)) you trigger yourself, not an automatic idle-detection stop. The only automatic lifecycle action is a fixed config.ttl timer that deletes the sandbox when it expires ('the sandbox is removed automatically when the TTL expires'), which is a hard TTL, not idle-based auto-stop.

windows.quote: A shell sandbox is a managed, isolated Linux container attached to an Agent Platform instance.
windows.note: All three sandbox types (Code Execution, Shell, Computer Use) are Linux containers; no Windows machine option is documented anywhere in the Agent Platform sandbox docs.

macos.quote: A shell sandbox is a managed, isolated Linux container attached to an Agent Platform instance.
macos.note: Same as windows: all sandbox modes run as Linux containers on Google Cloud; macOS is outside the product's scope (Google Cloud offers no macOS compute in this product family).
